sections.label: Enlistment Act 1967
sections.summary: The Enlistment Act was passed in 1967 when Singapore had little time to build its defence forces.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The Enlistment Act was passed in 1967, at a time when it was clear that Singapore had a very small window of time to build up its own defence forces.

sections.label: Committee to Strengthen NS
sections.summary: In 2013 the Committee to Strengthen NS consulted widely, made recommendations that were swiftly implemented, and NSmen felt the impact.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In 2013, the Committee to Strengthen NS (CSNS) started an extensive consultation process with a Steering Committee led by Defence Minister Dr Ng Eng Hen and two Working Groups focusing on Support for NS and Recognition and Benefits of NS.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: The CSNS committee came up with detailed recommendations which have been swiftly implemented and NSmen have felt the impact.

sections.label: Infantry-based NS training model
sections.summary: It asks whether the largely infantry-based training model suits NS in coming years given changing warfare and security threats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Yet, is this largely infantry-based training model appropriate for NS in the coming years, particularly with the changing nature of warfare and the security threats we face?

sections.label: Terror attacks on civilian populations
sections.summary: Terrorists aim to attack civilian populations in populated areas using basic weapons, making these threats harder to identify and prepare for.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Their primary aim is to attack civilian populations to cause as much damage as possible.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: They target highly populated areas, areas like train stations, airports, hotels and even gatherings.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Basic weapons − guns, makeshift bombs or sometimes even vehicles − can be used to carry out terror attacks.

sentences.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair (Sembawang)
sentences.text: In this respect, these threats are much more difficult to identify and prepare for.

sections.label: CSNS recognition and benefits
sections.summary: The CSNS report has many recommendations for NS, and the speaker supports more recognition and benefits, including insurance coverage.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The report by CSNS has many recommendations for the future of NS.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: I am delighted to support more recognition and benefits for NSmen, particularly life and personal accident insurance coverage for our servicemen.

sections.label: SAF Volunteer Corps
sections.summary: Another recommendation is establishing the SAF Volunteer Corps, proposed to include women, first generation PRs and new citizens.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: Another excellent recommendation is the establishment of the Singapore Armed Forces (SAF) Volunteer Corps which proposes to include women, first generation Permanent Residents (PRs) and new citizens.

sections.label: MINDEF MHA NSmen fitness report
sections.summary: The report suggested MINDEF and MHA work together to help NSmen keep fit and ready for IPPT.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira (Tanjong Pagar)
sentences.text: The report also suggested that MINDEF and the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) work together to help our NSmen keep fit and ready for their Individual Physical Proficiency Test (IPPT).

sections.label: NS Amendment Bill 1967
sections.summary: Dr Goh Keng Swee moved the NS (Amendment) Bill, passed on 14 March 1967, and NS began with 9,000 NSmen enlisted in 1967.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Dr Goh Keng Swee moved the NS (Amendment) Bill, which this House passed on 14 March 1967.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: With that, NS began with the first batch of 9,000 NSmen enlisted in 1967.

sections.label: NSmen in Cyber Defence Force
sections.summary: NSmen will be part of the 2,600-strong Cyber Defence Force over 10 years, and the Island Defence Training Institute will train over 18,000 NSmen yearly for homeland security.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: NSmen will be part of the 2,600-strong Cyber Defence Force over the next 10 years.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Every year, the Island Defence Training Institute will train more than 18,000 NSmen annually for homeland security operations.

sections.label: NS Square and NS50 tribute
sections.summary: The Prime Minister announced the Float@Marina Bay will be redeveloped and renamed NS Square, reflecting NS's central role in keeping Singapore strong and secure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: It is these precious and individual NS stories that make NS today part and parcel of being Singaporean in every family and uniquely Singapore.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: It is for these reasons and as a tribute to our NSmen, past and present, that the Prime Minister has announced that the Float@Marina Bay will be redeveloped into a permanent space and renamed the NS Square.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: Its permanence and prominence will reflect the central role that NS plays in keeping Singapore strong and secure.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: In this NS50 year, we can be proud of what we have achieved together.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Defence (Dr Mohamad Maliki Bin Osman)
sentences.text: If we can maintain this unwavering and strong support for NS from one generation to the next, then we can look forward to Singapore's future with optimism and assurance.
